application_criterion: Participant describes their own task as reviewing/correcting a draft rather than composing the analysis
Participant reports fewer or shorter reconciliation discussions between measurers
illustrative_quotation: We all start from the same draft, so we argue less about names. (M1)

application_criterion: Participant attributes tool errors or difficulties to weaknesses of the use-case text
illustrative_quotation: When the tool gets it wrong, the use case was often poorly written. (M4)

application_criterion: Participant values seeing the step-by-step analysis and being able to intervene at a step
illustrative_quotation: I can see why it counted that movement, and I can intervene at that point. (M3)

application_criterion: Participant reports time saved per measurement or per release
illustrative_quotation: A document that used to take me a morning now takes an hour of review. (M2)

application_criterion: Participant reports that the draft helped them or a colleague learn COSMIC conventions
illustrative_quotation: I used to apply the error-message rule from memory; seeing it applied each time helped me understand it. (M5)

application_criterion: Participant values that requirements stay on premises / under company control
illustrative_quotation: The requirements do not leave here. That was non-negotiable. (M1)

application_criterion: Participant reports that poorly written use cases degrade the draft
illustrative_quotation: The tool is only as good as the sentence it reads. (M4)

application_criterion: Participant reports variation in data-group / object-of-interest naming between draft and team conventions
illustrative_quotation: It is not that it gets the names wrong. It does not always use one name for one thing. (M3)

application_criterion: Participant anticipates effort to update prompts or examples for new domains or templates
illustrative_quotation: Every new domain needs its own examples, and I have to write them myself. (M1)

application_criterion: Participant reports the burden of operating the local inference server
illustrative_quotation: Keeping the machine running is my responsibility, and nobody had told me that. (M4)

application_criterion: Participant reports the need to stay alert because a wrong draft looks plausible
illustrative_quotation: It looks plausible even when it is wrong: that is the risk. (M5)
